feedback:
This candidate is a sound next test. It widens the sensor array to x = ±0.030 m with 16 mm footprints and raises kp to 6.0, keeping base_speed 1.4, kd 0.3, ki 0.05 and last_direction. Iteration 1 (base_speed 1.4, kd 0.3, kp 4.0, 12 mm sensors at ±0.016 m) ran off track on all 60 trials, with max_error 0.062 to 0.068 and about 2 line-loss events per run. Its rms_error (0.022 to 0.026) and steering_oscillation (0.13 to 0.19) were low, so the failure is line loss at the sensing edge, not jitter. That supports the sensing-envelope hypothesis: the outer sensors now reach roughly 9 to 50 mm of offset, versus about 0 to 34 mm before. I have approved it so it races, since the change is well motivated and there are 4 review and revision runs left. Nothing here states how it will perform.

What to change after the race, depending on the telemetry:
(a) If line_loss_events fall to 1 or 0 and max_error stays under 0.06 but progress stalls below 1, raise base_speed toward 1.6 to 2.0 and keep kp near 6.0. Iteration 1 showed slower speed helped only a little, so speed is not the main limit.
(b) If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with kp 6.0 and kd 0.3, raise kd toward 0.5 before lowering kp, because the widened array halves the signal per unit offset and therefore raises the effective gain.
(c) If line losses persist at the same bend entries with low oscillation, change controller.line_loss from last_direction to search_right or search_left, using the side that the bends favour. Iteration 1 showed that last_direction does not hold the line at entries.
(d) If the robot still leaves at bend entries after the sensing change, consider kp 7 or 8, but only if oscillation stays low.
